sources.entry: wanderer - Trail database where you can upload your recorded tracks or create new ones and add various metadata to build an easily searchable catalogue. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 Docker/Go/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: wanderer is a self-hosted trail database where you upload GPS tracks or create new routes and tag them with metadata to build a searchable catalogue.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes wanderer as a self-hosted trail database for recorded or newly planned GPS tracks. Users can manage their trails, plan new routes, and add metadata to build a searchable catalogue. It offers map integration and visualization, sharing trails with other people and exploring theirs, advanced filter and search, and custom lists for organizing trails. The README recommends installing with Docker Compose via a setup script that generates secrets, and also mentions a bare-metal option described in the documentation.
use_cases: plan new hiking or walking routes
how_to_run: /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL ...)" (setup script creates docker-compose.yml with fresh secrets; URL truncated in README)
Wait up to 90 seconds on first startup, then open the frontend at localhost:3000
If hosting not at localhost, change the ORIGIN variable to avoid CORS errors
Manual alternative: replace MEILI_MASTER_KEY, POCKETBASE_ENCRYPTION_KEY and POCKETBASE_PROXY_SECRET in docker-compose.yml before starting
notable: Self-hosted GPS trail catalogue with upload and route planning
Setup script generates fresh secrets for docker-compose
Sharing of trails between users and exploring others' trails
Custom lists and advanced search/filter over trail metadata
caveats: First startup can take up to 90 seconds
Requires correct ORIGIN configuration when not hosted at localhost to avoid CORS errors
Manual docker-compose setup requires replacing three secret keys before starting
